planting.note: Plant bare-root fans or potted divisions in spring or early fall, setting the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil.

directions: Part of Walters Gardens' Rainbow Rhythm series, this tetraploid daylily opens flat, ruffled pastel-pink blooms marked with a broad wine-purple eye and a matching purple picotee edge. Scapes rise to about 28 inches and rebloom after the early-midseason flush, with lightly fragrant flowers held well above the clump. Grow in full sun for the heaviest bud count, dividing crowded clumps every three to four years to maintain vigor.
sources: Walters Gardens Rainbow Rhythm variety catalog

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun, spacing clumps to allow air circulation and future spread.

directions: This Rainbow Rhythm cultivar carries a butter-yellow, peach, and apricot polychrome blend accented by a burgundy-red eye and matching picotee edge on 6.5-inch blooms. It flowers on tall, well-branched scapes in midseason and reblooms later in summer. Full sun and consistent moisture during bud development bring out the richest color contrast.
sources: Walters Gardens Rainbow Rhythm variety catalog

planting.note: Set divisions in spring or early fall in full sun; established clumps tolerate heat and humidity well.

directions: Hybridized by Rasmussen, this cultivar bears large, fragrant, pale golden-yellow flowers up to 7 inches wide centered with a bold raspberry-red eye. Its lower petals characteristically twist and curl into a swirling shape, giving the cultivar its name, and scapes branch well with up to a dozen buds each for a long midseason display. It performs best with full sun and reliable moisture through bloom season.
sources: Walters Gardens Rainbow Rhythm variety catalog

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun to light shade, dividing every few years to keep the compact clump floriferous.

directions: This compact Rainbow Rhythm tetraploid produces large, fragrant, light purplish-pink flowers with a heavy-substance eggplant-purple to merlot-wine eye and a matching picotee edge trimmed in white. Rounded, ruffled petals hold up well against heat and rain, and the plant reblooms after its midsummer flush. It performs reliably in full sun to part shade and stays tidy at roughly 24 inches tall.
sources: Walters Gardens Rainbow Rhythm variety catalog

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun; give plenty of room since flowers and clumps are large.

directions: A Rainbow Rhythm introduction with enormous 7-inch apricot-orange flowers, this cultivar features a wide orange-red eye repeated as a picotee edge along the ruffled margin, finished with a thin gold rim. It is fragrant and blooms in midseason on sturdy scapes that hold flowers above the foliage. Full sun and even moisture through the bud season maximize flower size and color saturation.
sources: Walters Gardens Rainbow Rhythm variety catalog

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun; this Minnesota-bred selection tolerates cold winters without special protection.

directions: Bred by Karol Emmerich, this Rainbow Rhythm selection produces massive, fragrant 6-inch raspberry-red flowers with a wide rosy-pink eye fading into a yellow throat, edged with a thin white margin. Flowers sit just above the foliage on proportionate midseason scapes and the plant reblooms later in the season. Its Minnesota breeding gives it exceptional cold hardiness alongside dependable bloom performance in full sun.
sources: Walters Gardens Rainbow Rhythm variety catalog

planting.note: Plant dormant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun; established clumps rebloom with light deadheading of spent scapes.

directions: Hybridized by Patrick Stamile, this dormant tetraploid opens pale-yellow, 4.5-inch flowers banded with a wide raspberry-red to maroon eyezone above a green throat. It is fragrant and blooms in early summer with a dependable rebloom later in the season. Full sun and average garden soil suit this vigorous, floriferous clump-former well.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun; semi-evergreen foliage benefits from winter mulch in the coldest zones.

directions: Registered by Patrick Stamile, this tetraploid daylily bears fragrant peach-orchid flowers just under 5 inches wide with a wine-red eyezone above a deep green throat. Semi-evergreen scapes reach about 25 inches and carry an extended midseason bloom period. It is part of Stamile's Candy lineage and shares that group's tendency toward bright, well-defined eyezones and vigorous garden performance in full sun.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun; deadhead spent scapes to encourage the fall rebloom.

directions: Bred by Patrick Stamile from a cross of 'Lady of Fortune' and tetraploid 'Janice Brown', this introduction produces strongly fragrant, trumpet-shaped pink flowers about 4 inches across with a red eyezone over a green throat. It flowers from early to midsummer and reblooms on 25-inch scapes. Grow in full sun with regular moisture for the best repeat bloom.

planting.note: Plant dormant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun, spacing to allow the well-branched scapes room to display.

directions: Registered by Patrick Stamile from a cross of 'Exotic Candy' and 'Magnificent Rainbow', this compact tetraploid opens cream to light-peach flowers washed with a violet-blue watermark that deepens into a fuchsia eyezone above a chartreuse throat. Scapes stay low at about 20 inches but branch well, carrying up to 20 buds through an early-midseason bloom with rebloom. Fragrant flowers and dormant foliage make it a reliable, cold-hardy front-of-border choice in full sun.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun; evergreen foliage may need winter protection in the coldest zones.

directions: Introduced by Patrick Stamile from a cross of 'Rock Solid' and 'Zahadoom', this evergreen tetraploid bears 5-inch lavender flowers with a blue-lavender eye, a fine silver edge, and a citron-green throat. Scapes reach about 30 inches and open early in the season with dependable rebloom. As a later addition to Stamile's Candy series, it carries forward the group's signature crisp, well-defined eyezones.

planting.note: Plant dormant divisions in spring or early fall in full sun; this diploid clumps readily and rarely needs division for vigor.

directions: Bred by Pauline Henry of Siloam Springs, Arkansas, this diploid daylily carries the Siloam name into a larger-flowered, heavily ruffled primrose-yellow trumpet nearly 5.5 inches across, with paler yellow midribs and a strong green throat set off by orange anthers. It blooms in early to midseason on 24-inch scapes, is fragrant, and holds an extended bloom period. Full sun brings out its clearest color and heaviest bud count.
